# 1525 — The Double-Gysin Infinity Jet Is Generated by Two Quadratic Channels

## Status

Closed all-grade formula for the codimension-two corner of Entry 1524.

## Two channels

Put

\[
A=(y_1+y_2)^2,
\qquad
B=(y_1-y_2)^2,
\qquad
z=X^{-1}.
\]

The exact iterated residue is

\[
I_{\rm corner}(X)
=\frac{2X}{(X^2-A)(X^2-B)}.
\]

After extracting its universal cubic falloff,

\[
\boxed{
X^3I_{\rm corner}(X)
=\frac{2}{(1-Az^2)(1-Bz^2)}.
}
\]

## Complete jet

Expanding the two geometric series gives

\[
\boxed{
C^{(2m)}_{\rm corner}
=2\sum_{p+q=m}A^pB^q
=2h_m(A,B),
\qquad
C^{(2m+1)}_{\rm corner}=0.
}
\]

Thus the infinite coefficient lens is generated by two quadratic channels,
not by independently chosen coefficients at every grade.

Equivalently, with (E_m=C^{(2m)}),

\[
\boxed{
E_m=(A+B)E_{m-1}-AB\,E_{m-2},
\qquad m\ge2,
}
\]

with

\[
E_0=2,
\qquad
E_1=2(A+B)=4(y_1^2+y_2^2).
\]

## Exact audit

The durable checker verifies the closed rational form, the parity projection,
and the recurrence data through (C^{(4)}). In particular,

\[
C^{(4)}=2(A^2+AB+B^2).
\]

## Meaning

The corner lens is infinite as a filtered object but finite as a recurrence
module: two source-derived quadratic channels determine every surviving
grade. This is a concrete instance of sector-specific coefficient thickness
being generated by a small carrier incidence algebra.

The result is intrinsic to the double total-energy residue. It does not yet
assert that a physical readout retains both channels.
